issues.description:
Retrying a Sent copy can send a new password to the previous IMAP server.

After an SMTP success and failed Sent append, makeSentRetry captures the old IMAP configuration and message. The account editor can replace the hosts, username, and passwords under the same account ID. Retry save fetches the current secrets for that ID and combines them with the old configuration. appendSentCopy connects using that former host and authenticates with the current password. This can disclose a saved credential to the previous provider after a mailbox migration. TLS authenticates the host in the captured configuration.

Source trace in mobile/src/services/mail/ebpMail.ts:139-171, mobile/src/screens/mail/MailAccountSetupScreen.tsx:205-223, mobile/src/services/mail/accountStore.ts:207-230, and mobile/src/services/mail/imap.ts:127-133 and :206-225. The existing retry test in mobile/__tests__/ebpMailSend-test.ts:73-84 keeps the configuration and secrets constant.

Reviewed at commit e252ae30e23b29328b678254c351359840f0cb49.

Mobile can move a different email after a folder's IMAP UIDs reset.

The listing drops the UIDVALIDITY returned by SELECT, and the message row passes only the folder and numeric UID into a new connection. The archive and trash paths ignore UIDVALIDITY on the second SELECT and issue UID MOVE. RFC 9051 section 2.3.1.1 scopes a UID to its mailbox and UIDVALIDITY value. After a server restores or recreates a mailbox, the old row can address a different message.

The real moveMailboxMessage function, driven by a scripted IMAP client, issued UID MOVE for the old UID after the mock SELECT returned a different UIDVALIDITY. The stub mapped that UID to a different message. This check used fixtures and reached no mail server. Locations are mobile/src/services/mail/imap.ts:240-257, :279-312, and :411-422, plus mobile/src/screens/mail/MailInboxScreen.tsx:313-329.

Reviewed at commit e252ae30e23b29328b678254c351359840f0cb49.

Removing a locked mobile mail account leaves its saved passwords on the device.

Remove account from device is available in the account editor while the identity is locked. deleteMailAccount removes the account record but only rewrites the encrypted vault when the identity's password is available in memory. The next unlock reads every entry from the vault, including the removed account's entries. A subsequent account update that rewrites the vault can remove them. The retention statement at PRIVACY.md:29 says saved credentials remain until account removal.

The real account-removal and unlock functions with stubbed storage and decryption removed the account row, left the vault untouched, and loaded the removed entry on unlock. See mobile/src/screens/mail/MailAccountSetupScreen.tsx:308-330 and :496-498 and mobile/src/services/mail/accountStore.ts:129-149, :174-196, and :290-301. Credentials in the residual file remain encrypted on disk.

Reviewed at commit e252ae30e23b29328b678254c351359840f0cb49.

Deleting a hosted mailbox on mobile leaves its signed address attached to the local identity.

Mobile signup saves a signed email detail on the identity, and the key server revokes that detail when the hosted account is deleted. After a successful deletion response, deleteEbpMailbox only removes local mail-account records. The unlocked profile continues to show the local entry because it merges those entries into the server view. The desktop deletion route removes the matching detail from its local identity after the same operation.

With a successful fake delete response and fake storage, the real mobile deletion and identity-detail functions removed the account and still returned the old signed email detail. See mobile/src/services/mail/ebpSignup.ts:340-369 and :549-599, mobile/src/services/details.ts:51-70, mobile/src/services/identityPublication.ts:37-54, server/handlers/mail-signup.ts:693-704, and gui/local-backend/managed-mail-routes.ts:702-716.

Reviewed at commit e252ae30e23b29328b678254c351359840f0cb49.

The printable Cardano confirmation can understate what the payer transferred.

Checkout review renders the amount and any additional ADA going to the recipient from the transaction builder. The printable Payment amount line reads only the original quoted asset amount. Cardano's minimum output requires additional ADA when a token is sent, and can raise the actual transfer when the quoted asset is ADA and the quote is below the minimum output. Confirmation currently runs on test networks.

With the real checkout functions and stubbed builder and DOM, a token review showed 1.04302 ADA going to the recipient and the confirmation showed only 2 tUSDCx. An ADA fixture reviewed 1.04302 ADA and printed 0.5 ADA. See website/checkout.js:315-325, :364-373, and :421-435, website/checkout.html:114-121, and server/payments/cardano_tx.ts:100-117. No wallet or blockchain call was made.

Reviewed at commit e252ae30e23b29328b678254c351359840f0cb49.

Mobile compose loads arbitrarily large attachments into memory before sending.

The document picker copies each selection and asks React Native FS for its entire Base64 representation without checking the selected file size or a total attachment budget. The resulting strings live in composer state, are serialized and parsed again by the send queue, and are wrapped into another complete MIME string. Large photos or video can consume substantial memory on the UI path and during send.

The real picker callback with fake file APIs asked for the complete Base64 content of a selection marked 150 MiB and added the returned attachment. The mock supplied only four Base64 characters, so this check exercised the path without measuring heap use. See mobile/src/screens/mail/MailComposeScreen.tsx:73-97, mobile/src/services/mail/sendQueue.ts:63-67, and mobile/src/services/mail/mime.ts:155-179.

Reviewed at commit e252ae30e23b29328b678254c351359840f0cb49.

Database startup scans payment history to repeat an already completed backfill.

PAYMENT_ORDER_SCHEMA_UPDATES includes an INSERT SELECT of every order with a transaction ID. Both database adapters run the backfill on each schema initialization, including after all candidate records exist. ON CONFLICT skips duplicate writes, but historical rows still have to be visited and checked. The SQLite path does this inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE and the PostgreSQL path runs it in the schema transaction. Startup work grows with the retained transaction history.

An in-memory SQLite database built from the checked-in schema showed SCAN mail_payment_orders for the original backfill on a second run against 128 previously migrated orders. That run inserted zero candidates. See server/db/payment-schema.ts:18-29, server/db/sqlite.ts:263-278, and server/db/postgres.ts:352-358. The PostgreSQL execution plan was inspected at the call site only.

Reviewed at commit e252ae30e23b29328b678254c351359840f0cb49.

Mobile CI can pass without compiling the Android release it is meant to cover.

The mobile workflow installs npm dependencies and runs Jest. Its STARTTLS regression mocks the platform upgrade and uses a mock react-native-tcp-socket connection. The Android app wires a separate Kotlin mail module and uses R8 in release builds. A broken package registration or release-only launch regression can therefore pass CI, as the automated checks never build the APK or exercise those paths. The project documents the previous minified launch crash and a manual device test for it.

Source inspection of .github/workflows/application.yml:27-37, mobile/__tests__/mailTcpClient-test.ts:1-18 and :74-107, mobile/android/app/src/main/java/com/mobile/MainApplication.kt:12-20, mobile/android/app/build.gradle:102-108, and mobile/e2e/README.md:104-143. The recorded issue concerns the current regression coverage.

Reviewed at commit e252ae30e23b29328b678254c351359840f0cb49.
